newsitem.title: BELARUS: Lukashenko wants NATO deal, Europe without U.S..
newsitem.headline: Lukashenko wants NATO deal, Europe without U.S..

text.p: Hardline Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko urged NATO on Tuesday to conclude a separate treaty with his country and said a new "European order" should be established without the United States.

"We are observing with interest developments in the dialogue between NATO and Russia, but Belarus's national interest also should be taken into account," Lukashenko told a gathering of Minsk policemen.
"I propose direct talks with NATO's leadership to sign a bilateral treaty between NATO and Belarus in the future," added Lukashenko, who once called the alliance a "dreadful monster".
The statement showed a shift in Lukashenko's policies towards talks with NATO, which intends this summer to invite several former communist countries in central and eastern Europe to join its ranks.
Russia fiercely opposes NATO's eastward expansion but is now focussing its efforts on clinching an accord with the Atlantic alliance that would guarantee its security once NATO expands.
Lukashenko, criticised by the United States and the European Union for a referendum last year that granted him sweeping new powers, is seeking much closer ties with Moscow.
But on Tuesday Lukashenko made clear his former Soviet republic of 10 million also wanted to be anchored within Europe.
"It's impossible to isolate Belarus. Belarus belongs to the fifteen biggest European states," Lukashenko said.
"We and only we, as members of the European family, can and must establish order in our own home without the participation of leaders from across the ocean," he added.
Last week the U.S. State Department accused Belarus of failing to uphold democracy and human rights and announced it was halting all U.S. aid to Minsk.
